title: f⁻¹ is not 1/f
hint: $f^{-1}(x)$ means the INVERSE function (the machine run backwards), not $\frac{1}{f(x)}$. Write $y = f(x)$, make x the subject, then swap the letters.

title: The order of fg
hint: $fg(x)$ means $f(g(x))$: the function next to x acts FIRST. So for $fg$, do $g$ first, then put the answer into $f$.

title: Inside the bracket moves the opposite way
hint: $f(x + a)$ moves the graph LEFT by $a$, not right: the new graph reaches each output $a$ earlier. Its vector is $\begin{pmatrix} -a \\ 0 \end{pmatrix}$.

title: f(ax) divides x by a
hint: $f(ax)$ is a stretch parallel to the x-axis with scale factor $\frac{1}{a}$: every x-coordinate is DIVIDED by $a$. Changes inside the bracket work the opposite way to what you expect.

title: The domain of the inverse
hint: Always state the domain of $f^{-1}$. It is the RANGE of $f$, not the domain of $f$: reflecting in $y = x$ swaps the x-values and the y-values.

title: Range is about outputs
hint: The range is the set of OUTPUTS, so write it with $f(x)$ (or y), for example $f(x) \ge 2$. Writing $x \ge 2$ describes inputs, which is a domain.

title: Reflect, do not delete
hint: For $y = |f(x)|$, the part of the graph below the x-axis is REFLECTED up in the x-axis. It does not disappear.

title: Modulus makes outputs positive
hint: $|f(x)|$ is never negative. Any point below the x-axis, like $(2, -3)$, goes to $(2, 3)$ on $y = |f(x)|$.

title: |f(x)| or f(|x|)?
hint: $|f(x)|$: the modulus is outside, so the OUTPUTS are made positive (reflect the bits below the x-axis). $f(|x|)$: the modulus is inside, so keep the right half ($x \ge 0$) and reflect it in the y-axis.

title: Inside or outside?
hint: A change OUTSIDE f, like $f(x) + a$ or $af(x)$, acts on y (up/down). A change INSIDE the bracket, like $f(x + a)$ or $f(ax)$, acts on x (left/right).

title: Which axis?
hint: $-f(x)$ changes the sign of every y-value: a reflection in the x-axis. $f(-x)$ changes the sign of every x-value: a reflection in the y-axis.

title: The order of transformations
hint: Outside f, follow the order of operations: for $2f(x) + 3$, multiply the y-values by 2 FIRST, then add 3. Doing it the other way gives $2(f(x) + 3)$, a different curve.

title: One input, two outputs
hint: A function gives EXACTLY one output for each input. If one input has two arrows (or a vertical line meets the graph twice), it is not a function.

title: Many-to-one is still a function
hint: Two inputs CAN share an output: $x^2$ sends both 3 and −3 to 9, and it is a function. What is not allowed is one input with two outputs.

title: The horizontal line test
hint: If a horizontal line meets the graph more than once, two inputs give the same output: the function is many-to-one, not one-to-one.

title: Only one-to-one functions have inverses
hint: A function has an inverse only if it is one-to-one. $x^2$ on all real numbers sends 3 and −3 to 9, so the inverse would not know which to give back. Restrict the domain, for example to $x \ge 0$.

title: Undo in reverse order
hint: To reverse a machine, undo the steps in the opposite order: for $2x + 3$, first subtract 3, then divide by 2. That gives $\frac{x - 3}{2}$, not $\frac{x}{2} - 3$.

title: Which square root?
hint: When you take a square root to find an inverse, check the domain of f. If $x \ge p$, then $x - p \ge 0$, so you need the POSITIVE root.

title: Check against the domain
hint: After solving, check each answer is in the domain. If $x \ge 0$, a negative solution must be rejected.

title: Two square roots
hint: $x^2 = 9$ has two solutions: $x = 3$ and $x = -3$. Always write $\pm$ when you take a square root, unless the domain rules one out.

title: Finding the domain
hint: For $\sqrt{\;}$, the inside must be $\ge 0$ (zero is allowed). For a fraction, the bottom must not be 0: find the x that makes it zero and exclude it. Watch the sign: $x - 3 = 0$ gives $x = 3$.

title: The least value is the y-coordinate
hint: For $(x - p)^2 + q$, the least value is $q$ (when $x = p$). The range uses that OUTPUT $q$, not the input $p$.

title: Check the turning point
hint: On a restricted domain, the least (or greatest) value of a quadratic may be at its turning point, not at an end. Sketch it: if the turning point is inside the domain, use it.

title: Key features of the graph
hint: Check the key features: $\frac{1}{x}$ has branches in opposite quadrants but $\frac{1}{x^2}$ is always positive; $x^2$ is a smooth U but $|x|$ is a sharp V; $x^3$ is an S shape.

title: Asymptotes and signs
hint: For $y = \frac{a}{x - p} + q$, the vertical asymptote is where the bottom is zero, $x = p$ (so $x + 2$ gives $x = -2$). The horizontal asymptote is $y = q$, the number added on.

title: Changing sides changes the sign
hint: When a term moves to the other side of the equation, do the opposite operation: $2x + 5 = 11$ gives $2x = 11 - 5$, not $11 + 5$.

title: x first, then y
hint: In $(x, y)$ the x-coordinate (input, across) comes first and the y-coordinate (output, up) second. To find f(a), start at a on the x-axis and read the y-value.

title: Square or round bracket?
hint: A square bracket $[\;]$ includes the end value ($\le$ or $\ge$); a round bracket $(\;)$ leaves it out ($<$ or $>$). Infinity always gets a round bracket.
